source.title: SAE-Xplainers: Rule-Based Feature Interpretation for Extreme Earth Events
source.authors: Hugo Porta; Emanuele Dalsasso; Chang Xu; Théo Gnassounou; D. Tuia

page_placements.theme: Validity of absorption and splitting metrics and detectors

record.tranche_reason: The study uses rule-set similarity and activation co-occurrence to identify SAE feature absorption, a different measurement approach from directly tracking a feature across dictionary sizes.
record.gate_note: The paper measures feature absorption using similar rule interpretations and co-occurrence, and reports example absorbed feature pairs. Its latent-dimension sweep (N: 4096 to 16384; k: 4 to 16) reports reconstruction and dead-feature results, not whether features split or absorption changes, so those results are not rows for the claim. It does not test larger-versus-smaller feature correspondences, input partitioning, or the effect of changing SAE objective.
record.test_reason: Feature absorption serves as a validation tool here: the authors argue that detecting it shows their rule-based SAE-Xplainers agree with SAE activations. The reported absorption and co-occurrence numbers come from two illustrative pairs that the method itself selected, plus trends in the method's own scores across Skope-Rules complexity settings. No parent–child hierarchy is established. Nothing measures whether a general latent fails to fire where a specific one takes over against a baseline. Absorption is not tracked across SAE size or sparsity: the Figure 7 sweep reports only R2 and dead features. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present GeoTopK as improving reconstruction and dead-feature rates. They claim SAE-Xplainers give faithful, literature-consistent rule interpretations. They say identifying absorption confirms the explainers agree with SAE activations. Absorption is treated as a validation check for their method, not as a finding about splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses GeoTopK and rule-based surrogate similarity/co-occurrence to identify absorbed features; it does not track features across SAE dictionary sizes or test parent-child input partitions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported absorption and co-occurrence scores vary with SAE-Xplainer rule complexity and dataset; for ClimateNet, co-occurrence is high at low complexity and decreases as complexity increases, while for SeasFire it increases with rule complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: In TopK/GeoTopK SAEs on a fine-tuned ClimaX model, the method flags pairs of features with near-identical rule interpretations and partial co-occurrence. Example pairs have SAEBench absorption scores of 0.19 (ClimateNet) and 0.22 (SeasFire).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Redundant or absorbed-looking feature pairs, detected via rule-surrogate similarity, appear in SAEs trained on weather and climate transformer activations.

record.problems: The absorption results use rule similarity and co-occurrence as proxies rather than directly measuring a parent feature's failure to activate where a child activates. The paper does not test whether changing SAE size or sparsity alters absorption. The illustrated absorption examples have no reported uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: The latent-dimension sweep in Figure 7 is not included because it reports reconstruction R2 and dead-feature rate rather than feature splitting or absorption. The co-occurrence score trend rows are included, but the plot provides no numeric values.

untested.parts: All: no tracking of features across dictionary sizes. Figure 7 (N 4096→16384) reports only R2 and dead-feature rate.
All: no splitting analysis at scale or across open SAE releases.
All: no nested families or geometric analysis tied to a concept hierarchy.
All: no established parent/child hierarchy and no measured failure of a parent latent to fire, compared with a baseline. No test of whether SAE size or sparsity changes absorption.
All: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents.
All: absorption is called sparsity-driven only by citation; no objective comparison. GeoTopK is compared only on reconstruction and dead features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and its V4 'supports' label are dropped. The absorption numbers are method-selected illustrative examples and method-performance trends, not independent measurements of V4. None of the cited originals is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Whether increasing dictionary size replaces a coarse feature with finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
Whether size-related splitting holds at scale or across open SAE releases.
Whether split features form nested, geometrically close families mirroring a concept hierarchy.

The study identifies absorption using rule similarity and co-occurrence, but does not directly establish that a parent fails to fire where a child takes over, or test whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes that behavior.
Whether larger latents decompose into smaller latents and whether larger SAEs add novel latents.
Whether splitting is an artifact of the SAE objective or whether another objective, such as Matryoshka SAEs, changes it.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study uses absorption detection as a check on its own method and reports no test of the claim.

tranche.reason: Absorption detection serves as a check that the rule-based explainers agree with SAE activations. Absorption scores vary with explainer complexity (Fig. 4b), not with SAE size or sparsity. The study does not test splitting across dictionary sizes. T4 fits.

source_check.notes: All four values appear only in Figures 15 and 16 and match the pack. They come from example pairs that the method itself selected (GeoTopK SAE-Xplainers on ClimaX). They are not evidence for or against any claim version. The N-scaling result (Fig. 7) covers only dead features and R2, not splitting.

statements.correction: SAE-Xplainers were trained on GeoTopK features of fine-tuned ClimaX (N=4096, k=4); see lines 653-657 and 755, Fig. 4, and lines 770-772. Groups are flagged by rule-set Jaccard similarity (M=50 closest pairs) and co-occurrence ratio >= 0.1. Example pairs: 3696/1670 on ClimateNet (absorption score 0.19, co-occurrence 9,800) and 3908/2342 on SeasFire (0.22, 4,763), Figs. 15-16.
statements.problem: The numbers 0.19 and 0.22 are correct. But 'TopK/GeoTopK SAEs' implies the absorption analysis ran on both SAEs. The SAE-Xplainers and the absorption analysis use GeoTopK features only; TopK is just the reconstruction baseline in Table 1. Pairs are flagged by rule similarity plus a co-occurrence threshold.
